title: Local constituent components: quantization surface and NVFP4 feasibility
scope: Survey of every locally-present constituent component of the VOID+Model stack for quantization feasibility, and a live measurement of NVFP4 (E2M1 weights, E4M3 16-element block scales) behaviour on Blackwell SM120 at the exact tensor shapes of those models. This run does NOT execute SAM 3.1 or VOID inference, does not produce masks or videos, does not quantify end-to-end segmentation or inpainting quality, does not download any checkpoint, and does not establish that any quantized configuration is fit for production use.

w4a16_vs_w4a4.finding: weight-only NVFP4 (W4A16) gives speedup 0.99-1.05x because the SM120 path dequantizes weights to BF16 before the GEMM; only W4A4 reaches the native FP4 tensor-core kernel
w4a16_vs_w4a4.kernel_evidence: torchao prototype mx_formats nvfp4_tensor.py dequantizes weight for the weight-only path; the native kernel appears only through torch._scaled_mm with both operands packed FP4

fp8_comparison.note: FP8 error is about 3.6x smaller, but measured FP8 GEMM speedup on SM120 was 1.12x (SAM3 trunk), 0.92x (CogVideoX proj) and 0.12x (T5-XXL, latency bound)
fp8_comparison.conclusion: FP8 buys accuracy, NVFP4 buys speed; they are not interchangeable

calibration_sensitivity.method: NVFP4 weight quantization at the four model layer shapes with global scale chosen from weight amax, 2x overscaled, and 0.5x underscaled
calibration_sensitivity.finding: for weight-only NVFP4 the per-tensor global scale is not the error driver; the 16-element block scale absorbs the outliers. Calibration of the weight global scale buys little.

activation_scale_study.setup: one outlier batch (20x) in the calibration set, activation per-tensor scale from calibration amax
activation_scale_study.finding: for W4A4 the activation global scale IS the error driver; a single outlier batch in the calibration set inflates the scale and produces up to 90% relative error. Trimmed calibration is mandatory.

decision_boundary_impact.method: thresholded mask comparison between BF16 and NVFP4-weight logits at realistic layer shapes
decision_boundary_impact.dimension_sensitivity: K=256..4096 gives IoU 0.9264-0.9376; wider layers are slightly better, so padding-free FP4 blocks do not fix the error
decision_boundary_impact.finding: NVFP4 weight error does not survive the segmentation decision boundary intact; a per-pixel mask changes on roughly 3% of pixels

support_detail.sam3: no torchao, no modelopt, no llmcompressor, no torch.scaled_mm, no quantization_config, no observer or calibration code
support_detail.void_model: no torchao, no llmcompressor, no modelopt, no scaled_mm. The model_cpu_offload_and_qfloat8 mode is not an FP8 compute path at all: predict_v2v.py:50 loads weights with torch_dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn and then predict_v2v.py:53 immediately calls .to(weight_dtype), where weight_dtype is bfloat16 from config/quadmask_cogvideox.py:61, so the FP8 dtype is undone before the first forward. The convert_weight_dtype_wrapper applied at predict_v2v.py:153 is therefore a no-op that only adds overhead. The one place FP8 weights survive, videox_fun/ui/wan_fun_ui.py:124, is dead code because that module imports Wan classes that do not exist in this repository.
support_detail.sam2_third_party: no quantize, int8, fp8, fp4, nvfp4, mxfp4, scaled_mm, bitsandbytes, torchao, fbgemm or modelopt anywhere in the tree

non_claims: No SAM 3.1 checkpoint was downloaded, loaded, or executed.
No VOID checkpoint was downloaded, loaded, or executed; no Pass 1 or Pass 2 inference was run.
No mask, quadmask, or output video was produced.
No end-to-end segmentation or inpainting quality was measured; the mask-boundary experiment used synthetic logits, not real model output.
The reported GEMM speeds are single-layer microbenchmarks at the models' shapes, not model-level throughput; attention, convolutions, normalization, and diffusion sampling overhead are excluded.
No quantized checkpoint was produced, and no calibrated NVFP4 artifact was built or validated.
The FP8 and NVFP4 error figures come from random-BF16 tensors, not from real model weights, so they bound the format's error floor rather than any particular layer's error.
The SAM 3.1 source audit and the SAM 2 audit are static source readings at the pinned revisions; neither worker loaded a checkpoint.
Hosted-API availability was researched from public model pages and the Hugging Face API, not by calling a provider endpoint.

hosted_api_finding.headline: Meta does host SAM 3.1 as a first-party API, contradicting the working assumption that no API exists
hosted_api_finding.input: short noun phrase plus an image or a video (H.264, H.265, or MPEG-4 container)
hosted_api_finding.output: one line per frame; each line carries a box and a binary mask per matched object
verification: GET https://api.meta.ai/v1/models returned {"error":{"code":"invalid_api_key"}}, which proves the endpoint exists and is live rather than 404
https://dev.meta.ai/docs/models lists sam-3.1 with input 'Text prompt, image, video' and output 'Boxes and masks'
https://dev.meta.ai/docs/media-segmentation documents the streaming request shape with an OpenAI Python client pointed at https://api.meta.ai/v1
https://dev.meta.ai/docs/pricing-rate-limits lists sam-3.1 at 3000 RPM with no TPM limit, and bills image segmentation at $2.50 per 1000 images and video segmentation at $0.20 per 1000 frames
hosted_api_finding.significance_for_samurai: The response carries binary rasters, so a hosted SAM 3.1 lane can feed the existing tensor-expert contract in src/samurai/ensemble.py directly, with no local checkpoint, no CUDA host, and no quantization work. The $0.20 per 1000 frames price makes whole-video segmentation cheap relative to a GPU run.
not_verified: No hosted endpoint was called with a credential; no MODEL_API_KEY is present on this machine.
Mask fidelity, latency, and video-tracking stability were not observed.
fal.ai SAM 3, Segmind SAM 3, and the other third-party listings were documented by the worker but not independently re-verified here.

corrected_findings: A source-only audit concluded that the VOID transformer parameter count could not be pinned because the checkpoint config was not reachable. The config was subsequently read directly from the live Hugging Face repo, which pins 42 layers at inner_dim 3072 and 5.57B parameters, and the safetensors header independently confirmed 5,571,094,144 parameters with 85.4% GEMM-shaped weights.
The qfloat8 finding was strengthened by execution: the FP8 load dtype is provably undone by the weight_dtype cast, so the path performs no FP8 compute.

The SAM 3.1 official checkpoint dtype was measured as FP32 rather than assumed; a third-party mirror republishes a file of identical byte length, and its NVFP4 artifact keeps the language backbone in FP32 while quantizing 54.0% of parameters.
